What this is

My Auto Racer is a drag race simulator for real cars. Pick any two of 2,900 models, set the distance, the surface and the weather, and watch them run — a full standing start with a Christmas tree, 60 ft, 1/8 mile, 1/4 mile, trap speed and a rolling speed trace for each car.

Every time is simulated, not measured. Each car is modelled from its published kerb mass, rated power, drivetrain and gearing; the model then trims tyre grip and delivered power until the car reproduces its own published acceleration figures. Both cars run in identical conditions — dry asphalt, 20 °C, sea level, 1 ft rollout — which is what makes the comparison fair even though no single time is a timing slip.

Are the times on My Auto Racer real measured times?
No. They are produced by a physics simulation, not by a stopwatch at a drag strip. The simulation is calibrated against each car’s published acceleration figures, so it agrees with the manufacturer where the manufacturer has published a number, and interpolates between those points everywhere else.
What can I change about the race?
Distance (60 ft, 1/8 mile, 1/4 mile, standing kilometre, or a roll-on), surface grip from dry to wet, air temperature, altitude, headwind or tailwind, gradient, passenger load, and a rolling start.
Where does the car data come from?
Kerb mass, power, drivetrain and published acceleration figures come from accelerationtimes.com and cardata.wiki, both CC BY 4.0. Kerb mass is recorded as the DIN figure — the car with no driver — and the simulator adds a 75 kg driver of its own.
Does it cost anything?
No. It runs in the browser, there is no account, and there are no ads.
My Auto Racer — a simulator. Real elapsed times depend on the track, the air, the tyres and the driver.

Disclaimer, cookies & analytics

Before you race

Every time here is simulated, not measured. Each car is modelled from its published mass, rated power and drivetrain, then fitted to its own published acceleration figures. The numbers are estimates. A real car, on a real day, with real tyres and a real driver, will do something else — treat these as a fair comparison between two cars, not as a spec sheet.

Not affiliated with any manufacturer. Marques, model names and badges belong to their owners and appear here only to identify the cars.

Race on a track. Nothing on this site is an instruction, an encouragement, or advice about how to drive on a public road.

Cookies and analytics. Nothing is stored on your device unless you say yes below. If you do, we keep two values in your browser — a random ID and your answer to this question — and send anonymous usage events to Mixpanel in the EU: which cars get raced, over what distance, which comparison pages get read. No advertising, no third-party trackers, no data sold, and nothing that identifies you. Say no and the site works exactly the same.

You can change your mind at any time from the link in the footer.
